advances: Ordinary convex surface measure and its normal conditionals. Applications to several mixed fibers can share a normal reference measure and require separate comparisons between physical conditionals.

proof:
The interval case follows from its two endpoint atoms. In higher dimensions the boundary is covered by relatively open graph patches of convex Lipschitz functions, and almost every boundary point is regular by the graph area formula and differentiability almost everywhere. The outer-normal graph is closed and the regular locus is Borel, since the sets of points with two normals separated by at least $1/m$ are compact. The unique normal is continuous relative to the regular locus, by compactness of the sphere. The probability disintegration over this Borel map exists on standard Borel spaces and is supported on the regular normal fiber for $\sigma$-almost every $u$.

If $p\in F_K(u)$ is regular with normal $u$, then every $q\in\operatorname{ri}F_K(u)$ has that same unique normal. Indeed express $q$ as a strict convex combination of $p$ and another point of $F_K(u)$ unless $p=q$. Any supporting normal at $q$ must also support at $p$, by equality in the convex combination of the support inequalities. Thus the regular normal fiber at such $u$ contains the relative interior and is contained in the closed exposed face.

The external input is L. Caravenna and S. Daneri, [The Disintegration of the Lebesgue Measure on the Faces of a Convex Function](https://cvgmt.sns.it/media/doc/paper/1434/disFacceConvCD.pdf), SISSA preprint 24/2009/M, §3.1, Definitions 3.1–3.2 and Theorem 3.3, (3.5)–(3.6), pp. 6–7, published in *Journal of Functional Analysis* 258 (2010), 3604–3661, [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfa.2010.01.024). For a finite convex $f$ on $\mathbb R^N$ and a Borel set $V$ of finite Lebesgue measure, the theorem disintegrates $\mathcal L^N|_V$ over $\nabla f$. For its gradient marginal almost every $p$, the conditional probability is equivalent to $\mathcal H^k$ on the projected gradient face intersected with $V$, with $k$ the affine dimension of that face. The paper uses a sigma-compact full-Lebesgue-measure differentiability domain whose gradient fibers are convex.

We choose such a domain that preserves the natural affine contact sets up to intrinsic null sets. Take countably many compact differentiability sets $D_i$ whose union has full Lebesgue measure, by inner regularity on bounded balls. The gradient is continuous relative to the differentiability set, by local boundedness and the closed subgradient graph. For $q\in D_i$ with $p=\nabla f(q)$ let $C(p)=\operatorname{argmin}_x(f(x)-p\cdot x)$. Adjoin all $tq+(1-t)z$ with $z\in C(p)$ and $t=1/j$ for positive integers $j$. Exhausting $z$ by compact balls yields a sigma-compact union: the condition $\nabla f(q)\in\partial f(z)$ is closed on each $D_i$ times a closed ball, and the combination map is continuous. Each new point has unique subgradient $p$ because any supporting affine function there also supports at $q$, by equality on the contact segment. At each retained $p$, the union includes $\operatorname{ri}C(p)$, since one can extend from a fixed $q$ through any point of that relative interior by a short amount. Its fiber is convex. Each combination of two retained points can retain a positive coefficient of one of their original $q$'s with the remainder in $C(p)$, and that coefficient can be decreased to some $1/j$ by convexity of $C(p)$. Taking $j=1$ includes the original $D_i$, so the domain has full Lebesgue measure. The projected gradient face therefore has the dimension of $C(p)$ and differs from it only on its relative boundary, which is null for the Hausdorff measure of that dimension. This choice avoids requiring an arbitrary ambient null deletion to be intrinsically null on prescribed faces.

For a boundary graph patch $P$, use rigid coordinates $\Phi(x)=(x,f(x))$, $x\in V$, with $K$ locally above the graph. Such patches follow by choosing a vertical direction from the boundary point toward an interior ball, so the point projects into the interior of the projection of $K$. Over that interior the lower and upper endpoints of each vertical interval are continuous, the lower function is convex, and the upper endpoint is strictly above the lower endpoint locally. Shrink to a bounded open ball $V$ with closure in the graph domain. On a slightly larger such ball, the graph function has uniformly bounded subgradients. The supremum of the supporting affine functions based there is a globally finite Lipschitz convex extension agreeing with the original on a neighborhood of $V$. Its gradients on $V$ are the local ones. This supplies $N=d-1$, a globally finite convex function, and a Borel set of finite $\mathcal L^{d-1}$ measure for Theorem 3.3.

Write $\theta(p)=(p,-1)/\sqrt{1+|p|^2}$ for the outer normal in these coordinates and $J(p)=\sqrt{1+|p|^2}$. The graph area formula gives
$$
\eta|_P=\Phi_\#\bigl[J(\nabla f)\,\mathcal L^{d-1}|_V\bigr].
$$
The positive factor $J(p)$ is constant on each gradient fiber. It changes the gradient marginal by multiplication by $J$ and leaves its conditional probabilities unchanged. The map $\theta$ is a bijection onto the lower open hemisphere. Thus the local normal conditional is the graph lift of the gradient conditional at $p=\theta^{-1}(u)$, and the local normal marginal is the pushforward by $\theta$ of the weighted gradient marginal. On $C(p)$ the graph lift is affine, with $k$-dimensional Jacobian $\sqrt{1+|\operatorname{proj}_E p|^2}$ for the linear space $E$ parallel to $C(p)$, with value one when $k=0$.

For a gradient occurring in the patch, a differentiability point lifts to a regular point of $F_K(u)$. The supporting plane of the graph at that point supports $K$ globally by convexity. Its intersection with $P$ is exactly the lift of $C(p)\cap V$. A nonempty relatively open portion of either convex contact set has the full affine dimension of that set, since it meets its relative interior. Thus $k=m(u)$, and the local normal conditional is equivalent to $\mathcal H^{m(u)}|_{F_K(u)\cap P}$ for its local normal marginal almost every $u$.

Choose a countable cover by these patches $P_j$. Let $c_j(u)=\eta_u(P_j)$. The normal marginal of $\eta|_{P_j}$ is $c_j\sigma$, and uniqueness of disintegration gives the normalized restriction $\eta_u|_{P_j}/c_j(u)$ as its conditional wherever $c_j>0$, modulo $\sigma$-null sets. Hence we may fix one full-$\sigma$-measure set on which every patch with $c_j>0$ has the asserted local equivalence, and the conditional is supported on its regular normal fiber. For such a $u$, at least one patch with $c_j>0$ meets $\operatorname{ri}F_K(u)$, by the cover, the local equivalence and relative-boundary nullity for convex sets. If a patch with positive conditional mass meets another patch at a point of that relative interior, their overlap has positive intrinsic measure there, and local equivalence gives positive conditional mass to the second patch. The unions of the positive-mass and zero-mass patches intersected with $\operatorname{ri}F_K(u)$ therefore form disjoint relatively open sets covering a connected set. Only the first union is nonempty. This gives equivalence on the entire relative interior, while every positive-mass patch gives zero mass to the relative boundary. The closed support is the full face because every neighborhood of a face point has positive intrinsic measure on that face. At a facet normal the fiber has positive surface measure and is the facet up to a surface-null set, so the conditional is normalized facet area.

For the common reference $\lambda$, the change of marginal formula follows by substitution, taking the kernel to be zero where $d\sigma/d\lambda=0$. An exceptional $\sigma$-null set is $\lambda$-null within $\{d\sigma/d\lambda>0\}$. For $\xi\le c\eta$, test the two kernels on a countable generating algebra of boundary sets and integrate over arbitrary Borel normal sets. Scalar domination gives $\xi_u(B)\le c\bar\eta_u(B)$ simultaneously for the algebra outside one $\lambda$-null set. The monotone class theorem extends this to all Borel $B$, proving the kernel domination. This supplies absolute continuity for selected surface submeasures on active faces.
statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body, $d\ge1$. Set $\eta=\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{\partial K}$ and $\sigma=(G_K)_\#\eta$, where $G_K$ is the almost everywhere unique outer unit normal, extended Borelly on its null exceptional set. Let $\eta_u$ be the conditional probabilities of $\eta$ given $G_K=u$. For $\sigma$-almost every $u$,
$$
\eta_u\ \sim\ \mathcal H^{m(u)}|_{F_K(u)},\qquad
F_K(u)=\{x\in K:u\cdot x=h_K(u)\},\qquad m(u)=\dim\operatorname{aff}F_K(u).
$$
Here $\sim$ is mutual absolute continuity. In particular $\eta_u(\operatorname{rb}F_K(u))=0$ and $\operatorname{supp}\eta_u=F_K(u)$. A singleton face gives a Dirac probability and a facet normal gives normalized facet area.

For any finite Borel normal reference measure $\lambda$ with $\sigma\ll\lambda$, the unnormalized conditional of $\eta$ relative to $\lambda$ is $\bar\eta_u=(d\sigma/d\lambda)(u)\eta_u$. For $\lambda$-almost every $u$ it is either zero or has the same measure class and support as $\eta_u$ above. If $0\le\xi\le c\eta$ for a finite constant $c\ge0$, the unnormalized conditional $\xi_u$ relative to $\lambda$ satisfies $0\le \xi_u\le c\bar\eta_u$ for $\lambda$-almost every $u$.
title: Disintegration of convex surface measure over outer normals
